# Brief — Internal tool rollout proposal (style verification deck)

This deck exists to exercise every bundled style with the same content. It is deliberately
neutral: a fictional mid-size company proposing to replace ad-hoc spreadsheets with a shared
request-tracking tool. All numbers below are invented and self-contained; there are no
external sources.

## Audience

Department heads (eight people) deciding in a 30-minute meeting whether to fund the rollout.
They have not seen the pilot data. Half will read the deck afterwards without the presenter.

## Message

The pilot cut request turnaround from 6.2 to 2.1 days; rolling the tool out to all five
departments costs 180k in year one and pays back in 14 months. Decide today so onboarding
starts next quarter.

## Constraints

- 10 slides, one claim each.
- No real product or company names; the tool is called "Tracker" throughout.
- The deck must work when read alone (titles carry the argument) and when presented.

## Facts (the only facts the deck may use)

- Today: requests are logged in 14 different spreadsheets across 5 departments.
- Today: median turnaround 6.2 days; 31% of requests exceed 10 days; 9% are lost entirely.
- Pilot (Support department, 12 weeks, 412 requests): median turnaround 2.1 days;
  4% exceed 10 days; 0 lost.
- Pilot satisfaction survey: 4.4 / 5 (n = 37), up from 2.9 / 5 before.
- Rollout plan: Phase 1 Support (done), Phase 2 Finance + HR (Q1), Phase 3 Operations +
  Sales (Q2). Each phase: configure → migrate → train → switch over, four weeks.
- Cost, year one: licences 96k, migration 54k, training 30k = 180k.
- Benefit, year one: 1,900 staff-hours recovered ≈ 155k; year two onward ≈ 210k / year.
- Payback: 14 months. Three-year net: +345k.
- Risks: migration of historical records (mitigated by keeping read-only spreadsheets for
  12 months); two departments use custom approval chains (configurable in Tracker).
- Decision requested: approve 180k and the Q1 start.
